## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(reshape2)
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library(corrplot)
library(reticulate)
```

```{r}
Data = read.table("Data_Projet_4modIA_2627.txt", header=TRUE)
head(Data)
```


```{r}
#| echo: false
dim(Data)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
Data$Smoking_Status <- as.factor(Data$Smoking_Status)
Data$Physical_Activity_Level <- as.factor(Data$Physical_Activity_Level)
Data$Alcohol_Consumption <- as.factor(Data$Alcohol_Consumption)
Data$Gender <- as.factor(Data$Gender)
Data$Family_History <- as.factor(Data$Family_History)
Data$Heart_Disease_Risk <- as.factor(Data$Heart_Disease_Risk)

summary(Data)

Data_quanti <- Data[, sapply(Data, is.numeric)]
Data_quanti

Data_quali <- Data[, sapply(Data, is.factor)]
Data_quali
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
apply(Data_quanti, 2, mean)
apply(Data_quanti, 2, sd)
```
```{r}
#| echo: false
boxplot(Data_quanti, main="Distribution des varibles", col="lightblue")

boxplot(scale(Data_quanti, center=TRUE, scale=TRUE), main="Distribution des varibles (centrées et réduites)", col="lightblue")
```
```{r}
On observe beaucoup d outliers pour les variables Weight_kg, BMI et Cholesterol_HDL.
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
corrplot(cor(Data_quanti),method="ellipse")
```
```{r}
#| echo: false
On observe que les variables Weight_kg/BMI, Diastolic/Syntolic et Cholesterol_LDL/Cholesterol_Total sont très corrélés positivement.

Les variables Weight_kg et Cholesterol_HDL sont corrélées négativement.
